title: Celownik · komu? czemu?
title_en: The Dative at last: to/for whom
note:
B1 Block 5 opener. The case behind the A2 pronoun chunks (mi/mnie: podoba mi się, boli mnie) — this unit gives the noun version. Two verbs that govern dative, both riding present classes already owned: pomagać (present_am, full 6-form paradigm — a genuinely regular verb, so nothing new on the verb side, only the case on its object) and dziękować (present_uje, partial spread — dziękuję was already a fixed social_chunk since trunk_social_a1; this unit is the first time it is analysed as a real 1sg verb form, and 3 more persons are added: dziękujesz/dziękuje/dziękujemy; dziękujecie/dziękują deliberately left untaught, load control, same partial-spread precedent as b1_conditional_sg's kupić/zrobić).

DESIGN FORK, logged (spine names three verbs — pomagać/dawać/dziękować — this pack ships two): dawać's present (daję/dajesz/daje...) is an irregular -awać class not covered by any present_* structure already taught, and adding a third new verb conjugation class on top of a brand-new case would stack two systems in one unit against the load-splitting rule. Conservative call: dawać is deferred, most likely to b1_giving (the vocab leaf right after this block) where 'giving' register already belongs and dawać/oddawać/pożyczać can be handled together. Flagging loudly for whoever authors b1_giving next — do not assume dawać is already covered.

SECOND DESIGN FORK, logged: the dative-noun side does NOT teach one general rule. Masculine nouns take the genuinely regular and near-universal -owi ending, demonstrated on two virile nouns already owned from the virile block (studentowi, nauczycielowi) — a real, generalisable rule. The spine's own headline examples (mamie, tacie, bratu, siostrze) are NOT this rule: mama/tata/siostra are feminine -a nouns whose dative/locative involves THREE different consonant softenings depending on the stem (m→mi, t→ci, r→rz — the same spelling machinery behind kobiecie, Annie, but never taught as a system in this course), and brat takes a small closed irregular -u set unrelated to -owi entirely. Deriving all of that honestly in one unit would be the same shape as the old do/z cliff (three-plus new alternations disguised as one lesson). Conservative call, matching how b1_virile_nom fenced its irregulars and how chciał/chciała were always handed over unexplained: mamie/tacie/bratu/siostrze are taught as FOUR MEMORIZED WHOLE FORMS, explicitly named as not following the -owi rule, not as a productive feminine pattern. The general feminine dative/locative -a→-e rule remains untaught after this unit — it is not on the current B1-SPINE as its own slot; James should decide whether it deserves one. Alternative considered: cut the family nouns and teach only the clean -owi rule. Rejected — family datives are the spine's named, highest-value payoff and are exactly the kind of irregular-but-essential vocabulary this course hands over whole elsewhere (kelnerzy, mógłby); a rule-only unit would be safer but poorer.

17 teaches_lemmas: the two bare infinitives (pomagać, dziękować — both genuinely new to the course, not reused, so tagged rather than left to uses_lemmas), 6 pomagać forms, 3 new dziękować forms, 2 regular -owi nouns, 4 memorized family datives. Subjects in Użycie use real nouns/names (nauczyciel, tata, Anna) with dative objects to keep the case contrast honest — the case lives on the OBJECT only, never the subject.

intro.title: Dative: the case behind mi/mnie
intro.body:
Since your early A2 days you have said Podoba mi się (it pleases me), Boli mnie głowa (my head hurts me), Smakuje mi (it tastes good to me). mi and mnie are the Dative case — the to me / for me case. It marks who receives something: who is helped, thanked, given to.

This unit gives you the noun version of that same case. Not just mi, but mamie — to mom.
intro.body_pl: Celownik = komu? czemu? (to/for whom? to/for what?). mi/mnie = ja. mamie = mama.

intro.title: pomagać — to help (+ dative)
intro.body: pomagać conjugates exactly like mieszkać — the pattern you have owned since the start (-am/-asz/-a/-amy/-acie/-ają). Nothing new on the verb. What is new is its object: you help someone TO whom the help goes, so the person after pomagać is always dative.
intro.body_pl: pomagać: pomagam, pomagasz, pomaga, pomagamy, pomagacie, pomagają. Pomagam mamie = I help mom.

intro.title: dziękować — you already own most of this
intro.body: You have said dziękuję since your very first lesson — it was a fixed chunk for thank you. It was never a verb to you. It is one: dziękować, the -ować → -uję pattern you already know from kupować/gotować. Here are three more of its forms, and its object works exactly like pomagać's.
intro.body_pl: dziękuję (już twoje) + dziękujesz, dziękuje, dziękujemy. Dziękuję tacie = I thank dad.

intro.title: The rule, and the four words that skip it
intro.body:
For most masculine nouns, dative is simple: add -owi. student → studentowi. nauczyciel → nauczycielowi. That rule is real and reusable on any regular masculine noun you meet later.

mamie, tacie, bratu, siostrze do NOT come from that rule — they are feminine words (and brat, an irregular case) with their own separate pattern this course has not taught yet. For now, take these four exactly as given, the same way you already took mógłby or kelnerzy whole.
intro.body_pl: student → studentowi. nauczyciel → nauczycielowi. mamie/tacie/bratu/siostrze: zapamiętaj całe.

quiz.explain: pomagać takes the to/for case — dative, mamie — not the accusative object you know from mam mamę.
tata is masculine but declines like a feminine -a noun here: tacie, not tatę (accusative) or tatą (instrumental).
brat's dative is the small irregular -u form, not brata (the genitive/accusative you already own) or bratem (instrumental, z bratem).
siostrze is dative (r→rz); siostrę is the accusative you already know, siostrą the instrumental from z siostrą.
Regular masculine dative: student + owi. studentem is instrumental (jestem studentem); student with no ending is just the bare noun.
nauczyciel + owi, the same regular rule as studentowi. nauczycielem is instrumental; the last choice has the wrong person on the verb.
you-form: pomagasz, same -am class ending you know from mieszkasz.
we-form: dziękujemy, the -uje class ending from kupujemy/gotujemy.
mama is the bare nominative — no case marking at all. pomagać needs the dative, mamie.
they-form: pomagają, from the same -ają ending as mieszkają.

type_items.explain: Memorized whole form — not derived from the -owi rule, which is masculine-only.
tata declines like a feminine noun in this case, despite being grammatically masculine.
brat is one of a small closed set of masculine nouns that take -u instead of -owi.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: The teacher helps the student.
use_items.explain: The case sits on the object only — nauczyciel (subject) stays plain nominative, studentowi (object) takes dative.
tata (subject) stays nominative even though it looks like an -a noun; only nauczycielowi (object) is dative.
